edges.description: Seeded organisms proliferate within the contiguous intervertebral disc and vertebral-endplate niche.
S. aureus adhesins and cell-wall factors contact osteoblast-lineage cells and stimulate JNK, TLR2, cytokine, and RANKL responses.
TNFR1-dependent JNK signaling contributes to TLR2 expression and RANKL induction in S. aureus-infected osteoblast-lineage cells.
Osteoclastogenic signaling contributes to inflammatory bone loss adjacent to the infected disc-endplate niche.
Local destruction allows contiguous spread into paraspinal and epidural compartments.
Local vertebral and discal infection produces the focal spinal pain that dominates clinical presentation.
Contiguous extension from the infected discovertebral unit forms epidural or paravertebral abscesses.
Epidural or paravertebral extension can compress or inflame nerve roots.
Direct inoculation establishes local S. aureus infection within the disc space.
The rabbit model develops vertebral and discal abnormalities after intradiscal inoculation.
Direct inoculation bypasses hematogenous seeding but can develop epidural involvement downstream of local disc-space infection.

nodes.description: Local disc-endplate infection presents with focal spinal pain in most infectious spondylodiscitis cohorts.

evidence.reference_title: Infectious spondylodiscitis: Epidemiology, diagnosis, microbiological findings, clinical features and outcomes in a 14-year retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: Back pain (79%) and fever (72%) were the most common symptoms.

nodes.description: Staphylococci proliferate across intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral bone, converting local seeding into infectious spondylodiscitis.

animal_models.description: Direct inoculation establishes local S. aureus infection within the disc space.
animal_models.name: Percutaneous rabbit disc-space infection

evidence.reference_title: Percutaneous inoculated rabbit model of intervertebral disc space infection: magnetic resonance imaging features with pathological correlation.
evidence.snippet: Disc space infections were present in all animals. MRI detected vertebral and discal abnormalities as soon as, respectively, 5 and 10 days after inoculation.

nodes.description: Local spread from the infected discovertebral unit commonly forms spinal epidural abscesses; the cited cohort groups epidural and paravertebral abscesses together.

evidence.reference_title: Infectious spondylodiscitis: Epidemiology, diagnosis, microbiological findings, clinical features and outcomes in a 14-year retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: Major complications included radicular nerve damage (51%), epidural/paravertebral abscesses (45%), endocarditis (14%), and a need for surgical intervention in 8%, with persistent neurological sequelae in 3%.

nodes.description: Infection extends contiguously into paravertebral muscles or the epidural space, producing abscesses that can injure nerve roots.

animal_models.description: Direct inoculation bypasses hematogenous seeding but can develop epidural involvement downstream of local disc-space infection.
animal_models.name: Percutaneous rabbit disc-space infection

evidence.snippet: These infections can often spread contiguously to adjacent paraspinal structures, including paravertebral muscles and the epidural space

nodes.description: S. aureus reaches the sterile disc-endplate complex, most often after bloodstream spread from a distant focus or after direct inoculation around spinal instrumentation.

evidence.reference_title: Infectious spondylodiscitis: Epidemiology, diagnosis, microbiological findings, clinical features and outcomes in a 14-year retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: Blood cultures were positive in 47% of pyogenic cases, 25% of all cases.

nodes.description: Fluoroscopy-guided inoculation of S. aureus into the lumbar disc of New Zealand White rabbits produces reproducible disc-space infection that can be followed by MRI and pathology.

evidence.reference_title: Percutaneous inoculated rabbit model of intervertebral disc space infection: magnetic resonance imaging features with pathological correlation.
evidence.snippet: Disc space infections were present in all animals. MRI detected vertebral and discal abnormalities as soon as, respectively, 5 and 10 days after inoculation.

nodes.description: S. aureus protein A binds TNFR1 on preosteoblast-lineage cells and activates JNK and TLR2-linked inflammatory signaling.

evidence.reference_title: Knockdown of TNFR1 Suppresses Expression of TLR2 in the Cellular Response to Staphylococcus aureus Infection.
evidence.snippet: Previous studies have demonstrated that the S. aureus protein SpA binds directly to pre-osteoblastic cells via tumor necrosis factor receptor-1 (TNFR-1).

nodes.description: Epidural or paravertebral extension can involve nerve roots and cause radicular neurologic injury in infectious spondylodiscitis.

evidence.reference_title: Infectious spondylodiscitis: Epidemiology, diagnosis, microbiological findings, clinical features and outcomes in a 14-year retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: Major complications included radicular nerve damage (51%), epidural/paravertebral abscesses (45%), endocarditis (14%), and a need for surgical intervention in 8%, with persistent neurological sequelae in 3%.

nodes.description: Microbiologically confirmed pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis can be treated with a six-week course of pathogen-directed antibiotics when source control and host factors are appropriate.

evidence.reference_title: Antibiotic treatment for 6 weeks versus 12 weeks in patients with pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis: an open-label, non-inferiority, randomised, controlled trial.
evidence.snippet: 6 weeks of antibiotic treatment is not inferior to 12 weeks of antibiotic treatment with respect to the proportion of patients with pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis cured at 1 year

nodes.description: Surgical debridement, decompression, or stabilization is reserved for selected spinal infection cases with neurologic compromise, instability, abscess burden, persistent bacteremia, or failure of medical therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Infectious spondylodiscitis: Epidemiology, diagnosis, microbiological findings, clinical features and outcomes in a 14-year retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: Surgical intervention is indicated in cases involving spinal cord or nerve root compression, instability, vertebral deformities, pathological fractures, or abscess drainage

nodes.description: TNFR1-dependent JNK and TLR2 responses in S. aureus-infected osteoblast-lineage cells increase RANKL, a pro-osteoclastogenic signal that can couple local infection to bone resorption.

evidence.reference_title: Knockdown of TNFR1 Suppresses Expression of TLR2 in the Cellular Response to Staphylococcus aureus Infection.
evidence.snippet: Knockdown of TNFR1 not only inhibited the JNK pathway but also reduced TLR2 protein and RANKL levels in S. aureus-infected cells.

nodes.description: Disc-endplate infection can erode adjacent vertebral bone and impair the structural disc-vertebra interface.

animal_models.description: The rabbit model develops vertebral and discal abnormalities after intradiscal inoculation.
animal_models.name: Percutaneous rabbit disc-space infection

evidence.reference_title: Infectious spondylodiscitis: Epidemiology, diagnosis, microbiological findings, clinical features and outcomes in a 14-year retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: The disease can lead to significant complications such as abscess formation and vertebral destruction, which may result in neurological impairments
